rv.q: Written in Scots, the play switches from a soft-target send-up of 18th-century acting to a two-dimensional debate about art and morality. The play is on fertile ground, but fails to settle on the characters and conflict that would give the factionalism of the early Scottish Enlightenment due dramatic weight.
Freewheeling romp through a famous episode in Scottish theatre
Logan and co with an irreverent yet respectful doff of the cap.
Despite the efforts of a versatile cast, the play never really takes flight.
